This is a small Node HTTP API — five files, no framework, no dependencies.

1. `server.js` — the entry point. Opens an HTTP server, checks the `Authorization` header, then hands the request off.
2. `auth.js` — checks bearer tokens. Each token is `<userId>.<signature>`, signed with HMAC and a shared secret from `AUTH_SECRET`.
3. `routes.js` — a small table mapping `METHOD /path` to a handler: list orders, get a user, or add an order.
4. `cache.js` — a 256-entry LRU cache that sits in front of reads, so repeat lookups skip the store.
5. `store.js` — the actual data, just an in-memory map. Every record expires 15 minutes after its last write.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  server -->|checks token| auth
  server --> routes
  routes -->|reads| cache --> store
  routes -->|writes| store
```

One thing worth knowing before you touch orders: the comment in `routes.js` says writes invalidate the cache, but `putOrder` never actually clears the cached entry. So after adding an order, `GET /orders` can keep serving a stale list until it ages out of the LRU.
